notes: FACT - Environment activation: /etc/profile.d/blitzy-cobolcheck-env.sh was present in this container and was sourced as the first command of the session, exporting JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64, JDK11_HOME, GRADLE_USER_HOME=/root/.gradle and a de-duplicated COB_CFLAGS. Recorded as an observation of container state only: this capture needs nothing beyond python3 and curl, both already on PATH, so no dependent value in this file is unestablished on its account.

FACT - Tooling was observed in this container rather than assumed, and nothing was installed: python3 reports "Python 3.13.7", curl reports "curl 8.14.1 (x86_64-pc-linux-gnu) libcurl/8.14.1 OpenSSL/3.5.3 zlib/1.3.1 brotli/1.1.0 zstd/1.5.7 libidn2/2.3.8 libpsl/0.21.2 libssh2/1.11.1 nghttp2/1.64.0 librtmp/2.3 OpenLDAP/2.6.10", jq reports "jq-1.8.1", and the gh CLI is absent from PATH. The capture was driven entirely by python3 urllib.request so that response headers could be read separately from response bodies, with no possibility of headers being spliced into a body.

FACT - The `authenticated` field was derived solely from the observed rate-limit ceiling returned by GET https://api.github.com/rate_limit: the x-ratelimit-limit response header read 5000 and was corroborated by resources.core.limit = 5000 in the response body. The unauthenticated control ceiling is 60 and was not observed. The presence of a token variable in the environment was never used as the basis for this field, because an exhausted unauthenticated quota returns empty response bodies rather than errors and would corrupt this capture silently instead of failing loudly.

FACT - The gate reading and the per-call readings differ, and both are recorded verbatim as observed rather than reconciled: _capture.rate_limit_observed holds remaining = 5000 with reset = 1786688052 as observed at the authentication gate, while each _capture.calls[] entry holds the value observed at that call's own instant - x_ratelimit_remaining 4965 then 4964, with reset 1786684750 on every call.

INFERENCE - The gap between the gate reading and the first capture call is consistent with two causes acting together: GET https://api.github.com/rate_limit does not itself count against the core quota, and the credential is shared within this environment so consumption between the gate and the capture is expected. Reasoning: across the capture the remaining values decrease by exactly one per request issued here, which accounts for this capture's own consumption in full and places the remainder of the gap outside this capture. The ceiling stayed at 5000 on every call, so the authentication determination is unaffected.

FACT - Comment pagination followed the Link rel="next" header to exhaustion rather than assuming a single page: rel="next" was absent from the first response, so the chain terminated with link_next = null on every recorded call after 1 page, returning 4 comment records in total.

FACT - Completeness cross-check passed: the assembled issue_comments array holds 4 records and the GET https://api.github.com/repos/openmainframeproject/cobol-check/issues/321 payload independently reports comments = 4. The two counts agree, so no silent truncation occurred and no discrepancy entry is warranted.
FACT - Issue #321 is a genuine issue and not a pull request: the payload returned by https://api.github.com/repos/openmainframeproject/cobol-check/issues/321 contains no `pull_request` key.
FACT - The issue payload reports locked = true with active_lock_reason = null, consistent with the upstream repository being archived and read-only, which is why this capture is not repeatable.

FACT - Observed metadata for issue #321: title "FR: please co-publish vscode extension on Open VSX Registry", state "open", labels [], created_at "2023-09-18T20:25:04Z", updated_at "2026-01-14T19:47:18Z". The title names the Open VSX Registry and co-publishing of the VS Code extension, which matches the characterization of #321 carried forward into this session.

FACT - The issue's updated_at (2026-01-14T19:47:18Z) is identical to the created_at of the newest captured comment (id 3751338621), so the thread's own newest record is what sets the issue's updated_at. The preceding comments are dated 2023-11-13T14:16:37Z, 2023-11-13T14:44:30Z, 2024-02-01T20:22:52Z. Nothing observed here contradicts the carried-forward characterization of #321 as an issue with recent activity.

FACT - The sibling harvest artifact upstream-harvest/issues.json was not available in this working tree at capture time (absent from the filesystem, absent from `git ls-files`, and absent from every git ref reachable in this clone), so the corroboration recorded in these notes was performed against the live GET https://api.github.com/repos/openmainframeproject/cobol-check/issues/321 payload - the same upstream endpoint issues.json is itself derived from - applying the same absence-of-`pull_request`-key filter that scanning issues.json would require.

UNKNOWN - Whether issue #321 is the *only* upstream issue with recent activity could not be established from within this capture, because that is a comparison across all upstream open issues and no cross-issue listing was read here. Both the comparison and its verdict belong to upstream-harvest/HARVEST-MANIFEST.md, so no ranking is asserted in this file.

FACT - Every HTTP request recorded in _capture.calls[] is a GET. No write of any kind - no comment, reaction, label, assignment, reopen or edit - was attempted against the archived upstream repository openmainframeproject/cobol-check.

FACT - Comment and issue payloads are stored exactly as returned: no field was pruned and no body was truncated, reflowed, re-rendered from markdown, HTML-stripped or whitespace-normalized. Each comment retains all 14 fields GitHub returned and the issue payload retains all 34, in GitHub's own field order. The issue body contains CRLF sequences; JSON string escaping represents each as the two-character escape \r\n, so the serialized file holds no raw carriage-return byte while every value still round-trips byte-identically.

issue.title: FR: please co-publish vscode extension on Open VSX Registry
issue.body:
Please add this useful extension to the [Open VSX Registry](https://open-vsx.org/?search=cobol).

Details on the publishing can be found at https://github.com/eclipse/openvsx/wiki/Publishing-Extensions.

A bit of explanation:
Open VSX Registry is the default extension provider endpoint for the free build of vscode VSCodium and Eclipse Theia, as well as browser versions like the one on GitPod. It would be nice to have this extension be directly published to a free vsix repository instead of only the Microsoft Marketplace with its restrictions.

You could also use a [GitHub action](https://docs.github.com/en/actions) that allows publishing to Open VSX and the MS market place, [HaaLeo/publish-vscode-extension](https://github.com/HaaLeo/publish-vscode-extension#readme) does this.
